what: Saturn and five of its moons, night of 17/18 October 2026 (frames of 18 October UTC)
telescope: Celestron 8SE, 203 mm, 2084 mm by plate solve

ephemeris.source: JPL Horizons, geocentric astrometric (ICRF), 2026-10-18 05:20 to 2026-10-18 07:26 UTC every 1m

selection.why_kept: plain stacks: 8 to 25 one plateau (within 3%), 5 sharper by gap contrast (0.145 vs 0.127); restored: 25 beats 5 (gap contrast 0.359 vs 0.313) with 0.0059 vs 0.0135 grain and Titan at 18 vs 8 sigma; checks/k5-vs-k25-rounds-0-8-12-20.png

titan_blur.note: colours were not slid in this tile: the red and blue offsets are the air's prism at Titan, to compare with step 5's on the planet

restoration.method: Richardson-Lucy on R+G+B, each colour scaled by the same ratio

record.name: Gaia DR3
record.epoch: positions at 2016.0 (ICRS); move them with the proper motions to the night

composite.planet_from: restored stack, 3x3 box mean, one linear resampling

steps.how: brightness changed, each pixel's colour ratios kept

steps.brightness: bilateral filter, sigma 4.0 px, 7 L units
steps.where: full below L 10, none above L 35 (brightness judged on a blurred copy)

steps.left_alone: below L 14 (fading in to L 30) and above L 93
steps.sky_without_colour: colour fades to grey below L 10 (full colour from L 22): the dark sky's colour is noise
